title: Playback speed you can pick: 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 4x and 8x
goal: The person wants to play a video slower or faster with a visible control, not only Premiere's J and L shuttle (which today steps 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x and has no slow speeds). Add a speed control to the transport with 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 4x and 8x; the picture and sound play at that speed, sound keeping its pitch; it does not change the edit or the export.
notes: User, 2026-11-12 (intake): 'Also another feature, I'd like playback to allow for speed control. .25x .5x 1 1.5 2 4 8x something like that?' Today: Sources/PhotonzCore/TimelineKeys.swift TimelineShuttle.ladder = [1, 2, 4, 8] (Premiere's J/K/L), no visible control, no slow speeds. Grown-up tools: Final Cut has no speed menu but plays slow and fast with J/K/L; Premiere likewise; QuickTime and YouTube show a speed menu with 0.25x to 2x, which is the pattern asked for.
acceptance: A speed control in the transport, beside play (a small menu showing the current speed, 1x by default), with 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 4x and 8x. Choosing one plays at that speed at once; it is remembered per window, not saved into the document, and never affects export.
Sound plays at the chosen speed with its pitch kept (AVAudioTimePitchAlgorithm or the audio engine's time pitch), up to 2x; above 2x sound is muted, as editors do, and the control says so.

Keyboard: the J/K/L shuttle keeps Premiere's ladder (1, 2, 4, 8) and shows its speed in the same control while held; Shift-period and Shift-comma (or the editor's convention, checked against Final Cut and Premiere and written down) step the chosen speed up and down.
At 0.25x and 0.5x every frame is shown (no frame skipping); at 4x and 8x playback skips frames to keep up and never falls behind the clock, measured on the reference edit from the video-perf work.
The playhead, the time readout and looping (in to out marks) all follow the speed.
Walks: pick each speed, play, the playhead advances at that rate within 2 percent; sound pitch kept at 0.5x and 1.5x (measure the pitch of a test tone); J L L shows 4x.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: owns these walks: playback-speed-walk, playback-speed-keeps-pace-walk, playback-speed-on-the-reference-edit-walk

Built: speed menu beside play (0.25x to 8x, per window, 1x default, never saved or exported), pitch kept 0.25x to 2x through one AVAudioUnitTimePitch, silent above 2x with a struck-through speaker on the control, Shift-period / Shift-comma and Sequence > Play Faster / Play Slower, J/K/L ladder unchanged and shown in the control. Chose: picking a speed while stopped does not start playing (QuickTime and YouTube do the same); picking while playing changes speed in place, keeping the direction. Chose L L L over the checklist's J L L for the 4x check: with Premiere's ladder J then L restarts at 1x forwards.

Measured (walks playback-speed-walk, playback-speed-keeps-pace-walk, playback-speed-on-the-reference-edit-walk): tone 440.1 Hz at 1x, 440.3 at 0.5x, 439.6 at 1.5x; playhead pace on the 5 min Retina talk 0.249/0.500/1.000/1.496/1.995/4.062/7.994x; every look at 0.25x and 0.5x shows the frame under the playhead; 4x and 8x within 3 frames there. On the reference edit 0.5x and 4x pass. NOT REACHED: 8x on the 6 min reference edit falls up to 185 frames behind (looks 4 to 24); the forward pass restarts from its key frame faster than it can deliver (fallenBehind is 12 grid frames at 8x, about 50 ms of the clock). Next step: at speeds above 2x, open the restarted pass ahead of the playhead by the decode start-up (about 0.4 s of the clock) and let serves() accept a pass the playhead has not reached yet. Task left pending for this; the walk playback-speed-on-the-reference-edit-walk is this task's and fails at its 8x step until then.

Left rough, not filed: 2x from rest on the Retina talk held one look 4 frames behind at 0.14 s in 1 of 3 runs (start-up decode; 2x has sound, so it does not pre-roll). Filed separately: a-picked-sound-clip-draws-no-size-badge-or-handl (a 0 x 0 badge on the canvas for a picked sound, seen in this walk's pictures). Folded CI red (TextRevealUnclippedTests, run 43467774822) into find-out-why-the-legibility-check-once-read-the. Shared code note: the speed menu lives in the shared TimelineDock, reached only through the document timeline that Next opens recordings into.

Shipped the speed menu, pitch-kept sound, keys and walks (0c0b3edf8); every acceptance item verified except 8x on the six minute reference edit, which still falls up to 185 frames behind. Left open for that one bar; next step is in the log.

Reproduced the 8x bar first: playback-speed-on-the-reference-edit-walk failed at 8x, 21 of 24 looks late, up to 177 behind. Traced every pass open/stop: (1) serves() asked for the playhead's own frame at 8x where only every third is kept, so passes ahead of the playhead restarted two ticks in three; (2) the same in plan's reaches() tore down the primed far side of each cut every tick; (3) every decode-width change during a zoom cancelled every pass, and cancelled passes held the sweep gate; (4) the reference recordings are 60fps H.264 with B-frames, so 8x needs 480 decodes/s of a decoder that does ~630 total (bench). Fixed all four: kept-frame checks with an in-flight margin, any size serves above 2x, and above 2x passes decode through VideoToolbox skipping unreferenced samples (~half; bench 632 -> 1199 frames/s). Plus restart startLead ahead above 2x, comingLead in clock time, prime by stride. Tested first in MoviePlayPassTests, MovieDecodeReorderTests.

Chose letting a pass read at another size go on above 2x over restarting it at each size, because a zoom at 8x is an eighth of a second on screen and restarting stuck the picture; frames can look soft during a fast zoom until the playhead stops. Chose not to widen the fallen-behind limit (tried max(12, startLead): fewer restarts but more looks behind).

Fixed two flaky measurements in this task's own walks rather than loosening them: the pace check now allows the one 33ms clock tick a look can find the playhead stale by (0.5x read 0.514x twice on an exact clock), and TonePitch no longer reads an uneven 440 tone at 220.1 Hz (2 of 5 runs of playback-speed-walk at 1.5x); both with unit tests.

8x now keeps up on the six minute reference edit (every look within 3 frames, pace 7.96 to 8.07x, 6 runs of 6; was up to 185 behind): above 2x passes decode only the frames other frames depend on (VideoToolbox, ~2x decoder throughput), kept-frame checks no longer restart passes ahead of the playhead, zooms no longer restart passes. Walk pace and pitch readers made robust (pace through every look; no octave-down misread). Commit ad24392f4; all three walks green, full Scripts/test.sh green.
